question.text: Yamuna Credit Opportunities AIF (Cat II) is appointing a Fund Administrator. Which of the following is NOT typically a core function of a Fund Administrator?

answer.text: Independent DUE DILIGENCE of PPM disclosures and issuance of due-diligence certificate for SEBI filing
NAV calculation, valuation services and risk reporting
Maintenance of funds books and records, income/expense accruals, and tax-reporting solutions
Preparing manual and electronic payment instructions to settle fund expenses; daily reconciliation

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the workbook, the Fund Administrator's core functions include maintenance of books and records, income/expense accruals, tax and regulatory reporting, NAV calculation, valuation services, risk reporting, payment instructions, reconciliation, financial reports, and audit support. Independent due diligence of PPM disclosures and issuance of the due-diligence certificate for SEBI filing is performed by the Merchant Banker, not the Fund Administrator. The Trap: The three non-keyed options each describe activities the workbook explicitly attributes to the Fund Administrator. The keyed option correctly identifies the Merchant Banker's PPM due-diligence function as outside the Fund Administrator's scope. Note: Service-provider roles (Fund Administrator, Custodian, Merchant Banker, Auditor) are deliberately separated in the AIF ecosystem; do not blur them when describing operational responsibilities.
